description: Change of use of the existing House in Multiple Occupation (Use Class C4) occupied by up to six persons to a large House in Multiple Occupation (Sui Generis) occupied by up to eight persons, with no internal changes.

phasing_details.phase_detail: Conversion of rooms 4 and 5 completed in one phase

decision_conditions:
Condition : 1 - The development hereby permitted shall begin not later than three years from the date of this decision.
Reason: In order to comply with Section 91 of the Town and Country Planning Act 1990, as amended by Section 51 of the Planning and Compulsory Purchase Act 2004.
Condition : 2 - The development hereby permitted shall be carried out in accordance with the following approved plans and specifications: Unnumbered Block/Site plan, Unnumbered location plan, 111/01/103; Received: 29/07/2026. 111/01/102 A, 111/01/104; Received: 31/07/2026. 111/01/101 A; Received 18/09/2026.
Reason: In order to ensure the development is carried out in accordance with the planning permission.
Condition : 3 - Before the development hereby permitted is first occupied or brought into use, full details (including manufacturers' specifications (for not less than eight (8) bicycles) of secure covered cycle parking facilities that accord with the West London Cycle Parking Guidance shall be submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority. The approved facilities shall be fully implemented and made available for use before the development is first occupied or brought into use, The approved facilities shall be thereafter retained for use at all times without obstruction.
Reason: In order to support sustainable transport objectives.
Condition : 4 - Before the development hereby permitted is first occupied or brought into use, the Local Planning Authority shall be informed so that arrangements can be put in place to ensure that, with the exception of a person eligible for a disabled person's badge issued pursuant to section 21 of the Chronically Sick and Disabled Persons Act 1970 (or similar legislation), no resident of the development shall obtain a resident's parking permit. Any occupiers of the approved development shall surrender any such permit wrongly issued or held.
Reason: In order to protect the free flow and safety of traffic on nearby highways and to support sustainable transport objectives.
Condition : 5 - The refuse and recycling store shall be completed and made available for use before the development hereby permitted is first occupied or brought into use following the requirements set in the West London Waste Plan and the Council's Recycling and Refuse guidance, and thereafter shall be retained for such use at all times without obstruction. The developer shall provide a set of containers adequate for the House in Multiple Occupation use for the storage and collection of recyclable materials for the purposes of the Council's kerbside recycling service, to the specification of the local authority's recycling collection service. The waste and recyclable materials containers shall be stored in a proprietary refuse bin designed for the purpose to be supplied by the developer and located within the premises. Besides, the development shall also supply a garden waste composting bin following the aforementioned policies and guidelines.
Reason: In order to ensure adequate provision for waste and recycling.
Condition : 6 - The development hereby approved shall be occupied by no more than eight (8) persons at any one time.
Reason: In order to protect neighbours' living conditions and the character of the area.
Condition : 7 - Prior to the commencement of the approved use, an HMO Management Plan shall be submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority. The Plan shall set out the arrangements for the day-to-day management and maintenance of the property in accordance with the Management of Houses in Multiple Occupation (England) Regulations 2006. The approved Plan shall thereafter be implemented and maintained for the lifetime of the development.
Reason: In order to protect neighbours' living conditions and the character of the area.
